"Pupils are rightly very proud of their school and their achievements. They enjoy coming to this welcoming and friendly school and appreciate all aspects of school life"
Pupils’ well-being is paramount and as a result pupils feel safe. Staff know the pupils very well and there are strong and trusting relationships. Pupils know that staff will listen to them if they have any worries or concerns. Expectations are very high. All pupils, including disadvantaged pupils and pupils with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND), are challenged to achieve their very best academically and personally.

PE and Sports Funding
The Primary PE and Sports Premium was introduced to improve the provision of physical education and school sports in primary schools across England. The funding may only be spent on improving the provision of PE and sports in schools.
Please read the information below which gives details of our PE and Sport Premium Grant and how we allocate the funding.

Royal Shakespeare Company Mentor School for the School Association Partnership
We are really proud to be chosen to be a Mentor school for the Royal Shakespeare Company's Associate Schools Programme in partnership with The Marlowe Theatre and the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC). In 2024 we signed up to a further 5 years in order to ensure this programme continues to enrich our curriculum offer and out of school activities. The programme is targeted towards schools who want to develop and improve access to Shakespeare, and to deliver the best teaching in the classroom through active drama techniques.
Through the Associate Schools Programme we have received fantastic development training for teachers and rich cultural and learning experiences for our children. We are proud to be regarded as a strong partnership school and were the only school chosen to perform at the Marlowe Theatre’s Annual Supporters dinner 2019.
All year groups take part in Shakespeare workshops led by our Shakespeare Club Lead and Creative Arts Provider. These workshops develop our children’s speaking and listening skills, curiosity for language, use of ambitious words and builds confidence. Children learn to read scripts and use this rich language in their writing.

Late/Absence Procedures
Pupil Attendance Guidance for Parents
Ethelbert Road Primary School recognises the importance of good attendance and punctuality and the negative impact of poor attendance and punctuality on a child’s learning. We are therefore committed to ensuring that, as an organisation, we do everything we can to improve our pupils’ attendance and punctuality.
We regularly monitor the attendance and punctuality of our pupils and work hard to send a clear message to parents that we are committed to high levels of attendance and punctuality and will vigorously challenge those children, and their parents who are ultimately responsible, who fail to meet our high expectations.
Children are at school for 190 days in a school year; it is our school’s hope that parents will support their children’s full attendance. Holidays, birthday treats, theatre visits etc. need to be planned for outside school time. The term dates are sent home well in advance so that parents are able to take these into account when planning holidays.
If your child is going to be late, please try to phone ahead and notify the office. Once you have arrived at school please fill in the late form on our electronic system. Lateness will be carefully tracked and if your child is continuously late you will be invited to attend a meeting to see if the school can help.

Wraparound Care
Wraparound Care Staff
Headteacher supported by the Office Manager
WRAPAROUND CARE (Breakfast club and After School Care)
Ethelbert Road Primary School, breakfast and after school care currently provides wraparound care provision for all children attending the school (if spaces available and up to 30 children per session).
These operate daily providing continuous care within the school setting from 7.55am to 5.30pm.
Both clubs are becoming increasingly popular, so In order to ensure that we have sufficient staff we do need to know in advance which days the children will be attending. Regular places must be booked in advance and by Thursday 3pm, for the following week. Additional and ad-hoc sessions may be booked, dependent on availability. 24 hours’ notice will be required. This is so that we can ensure we have the appropriate adult to child ratios whilst giving our staff plenty of notice.
Breakfast Club is open from 7.55am every morning, with breakfast is served until 8.30am. After School Club is open from 3.15pm until 5.30pm Monday - Friday. Please note that staff are only present until 5:30pm, so if you are running late please could you telephone the After School Club (the main office closes at 4pm) or arrange for someone else to collect.
In addition to providing childcare the club offers an excellent opportunity for the children to engage and socialise with their peers. During the time spent at the club children can choose from a variety of planned activities including messy play, creative activities, free and structured play within the indoor and outdoor environment.
Some staff work in both breakfast club and after school care enabling continuity of care.
Meal times are an important time for children to socialise. Children at Breakfast Club are offered a choice of cereal, toast, fruit or yoghurt.
At after school care, the children are provided with fruit, drinks and a light snack.
All food conforms to school food guidelines. All allergies/intolerances should be notified to staff via the school office.
Fees – Breakfast Club = £3.00 per session per child
Fees – After-school Club =£5.00 per session per child up to 4.30pm and £9.00 per session per child up to 5.30pm.
If your child attends a school paid club before needing after school care, the cost for this remaining after school care session 4.15pm – 5.30pm will be £5.00.
If they attend a school club that is free, you will need to pay for the whole after school care session up to 5.30pm £9.00.
Fees are payable in advance by either payment directly into the account or by cheque or cash into the school office. We also accept childcare vouchers. If you require more information on how to use childcare vouchers, please speak to someone in the school office.
Fees will be reviewed annually during the Summer Term and parents/carers will be notified of any changes.
The Breakfast and After School Care can be contacted during opening hours on 07716137238 or via the main school office between 8am and 4pm 01795 533124.

Young Carers
At Ethelbert Road Primary School, we are committed to recognising and supporting the unique challenges faced by young carers.
We understand that caring responsibilities can have a significant impact on a child's education, wellbeing, and development, and we strive to create a fully inclusive school culture where every child feels valued, understood, and supported. We work closely with young carers and their families to ensure they can enjoy school, achieve their full potential, and access the same opportunities as their peers.
Through early identification, pastoral support, flexible approaches where needed, and signposting to specialist services and local young carers' organisations, we help children and families access the support they need.
Our aim is to promote positive wellbeing, reduce barriers to attendance and learning, and equip young carers with the confidence, skills, and resilience they need to be successful in school and better prepared for independent adult lives.
By fostering an accessible, understanding, and supportive environment, we ensure that young carers are able to thrive both academically and personally.
If you require more information about young carers, please feel free to speak to the Headteacher, or Deputy Headteacher/SENCo.
